title: The Strangers
full_review:
That 4 a.m. knock on the door isn't the Avon lady; it's "The Strangers" (Universal/Rogue).

When Kristen (Liv Tyler) and her preppy beau, James (Scott Speedman), return from a friend's wedding at which Kristen declined her boyfriend's proposal, they're set to spend the night at his parents' isolated summer home alternately moping and working through their problems. But they're interrupted by that untimely rapping and a shadowy visitor asking randomly, "Is Tamara here?"

This mysterious apparition turns out to be the prelude to hours of terror as the couple is relentlessly menaced by a trio of masked intruders (Gemma Ward, Kip Weeks and Laura Margolis). Their car is trashed, their cell phones are disabled and eventually, of course, the electricity is cut.

Before its grisly climax, writer-director Bryan Bertino's reasonably taut feature debut mostly eschews bloodletting in favor of old-fashioned chills. But the script leaves many questions unanswered (Tamara, as they say, never comes), and its brief foray into religion and morality -- via the criminals' encounter with a pair of young Mormon missionaries -- falls flat.

The film contains some bloody violence, nongraphic premarital sexual activity, some rough and occasional crude language, and two uses of profanity. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is L -- limited adult audience, films whose problematic content many adults would find troubling. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted. Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian.
